Memory IBetween us

How it started

That first photo

My mom sent me a photo of you on a day I had no reason to remember. Your family wanted to know if ours might say yes.

I spoke to your chitappa first. Then you and I started talking. I had questions from the life I’d lived before. My mom gave me time to choose. She said we’d make a proper circle.

I took my questions to my favorite God. I felt like I got a sign. ‘Go. Say yes to her.’ So I did.

Memory IIBetween us

Our wedding and our first year

Four days before the wedding

Four days. That’s how long we’d known each other in person when we said yes again, this time at our wedding.

I hoped I’d be the man your family had told you about. Then you came here, and we started figuring out how to live our lives together.

We cuddled. We quarreled. We both had opinions about everything. I smile at how much fun I had getting to know the woman I’d just married.

Memory IIIBetween us

October 2019

What I carried from that October

That October shook us. By Diwali there was a little joy again. Some of the fear came with us, too.

In those days I felt closer to you. I made a few quiet promises to myself about being someone you could count on.

I was still learning how much of that begins with asking what you need and really listening.

Memory IVBetween us

2020

Your first proper snowfall

You saw your first proper snowfall. The wish you’d prayed for came true. Then came March, and the world went into lockdown.

Sometimes I think God gave us those ten months. You and me, inside those four walls. They were some of the happiest months I’ve had with you.

Memory VBetween us

Interlude

If I could borrow a day

If I could borrow a day from all the years we’ve had, I’d pick an ordinary one from those months inside our four walls.

Just you and me, and the whole day ahead of us.

Memory VIBetween us

October 20, 2020

The day we met our first son

More than thirty hours in the labor ward. And then there he was. Our first son.

I remember how much joy he brought you. I felt it too, just being there with the two of you.

We had so much to learn about being parents. Even now, thinking about the day we became three makes me smile.

Memory VIIBetween us

The years that followed

A new home and a lot to figure out

The years went by in a rush. Parenting, work, a new home, one trip to India. There was so much to be happy about.

There were times I let you down. There were moments, while we were learning how to be parents, when you needed me beside you. I fell short.

07 / 13

Memory VIIIBetween us

Building a career

Finding your way

Somewhere in those years, a question started coming up when we talked. ‘What am I?’ You were trying to build a career of your own, and I could see how much it was asking of you.

To me, it felt like God had other plans, like He was testing you along the way. It took money and patience, effort and sacrifice from you, with family pressure piling up, too.

And there was plenty to celebrate. Your first driver’s license, for one. You started driving, and before long you’d drive just about anything. Look at you now, the racer.

You went out and found a job on your own. You made it work. You were doing great. Some plans worked out. Some fell through. You kept trying new ones.

You picked out the furniture that made this place feel like home. You made friends and brought new people into our lives. I was proud to see all the things you were making happen.

Memory IXBetween us

Around 2023

When he turned three

When our eldest turned three, he started making friends. We got to know whole new families because of the friends he found.

I was trying to keep up with work. You were studying, going to college, and applying for opportunities. We were figuring out how to raise him, how to keep him busy, how to make time for the friends he’d found.

And then you broke your leg. I still remember those shoes you wore with the cast. Oh my God. That was a lot to get through on top of everything you were carrying.

09 / 13

Memory XBetween us

2024

Staying together

We had a lot to say in 2024. Some of it came out heated. We both had our reasons. We heard some things differently. A lot of conversations stopped before we got to the end of them.

Through all of that, staying together was something we were sure of.

I remember our road trips that year, too. Florida, then Florida again. Back to Nashville. And all those miles we put in around Georgia and Alabama. We did most of our roaming right here.

We’re mountain people, you and me. We’ve never been shy of a beach, either. Long after the drive home, there was still sand in our pockets.

10 / 13

Memory XIBetween us

December 2025

Then there were four of us

Then came 2025. We decided to make it a bit bigger. Bigger chaos. Bigger noise. And a bigger family.

It was easy for me to say, “Let’s have another.” Getting ready was harder. Some days those five years fell away and I was back in that room with you, waiting for our first boy.

There were moments then when you needed me. I can’t go back and stand beside you in them. This time I made you a promise. I hope I kept it in the ways you needed.

I hope you had moments that were yours, when what you wanted came first and you could see the world your own way.

You knew what labor had asked of you before. You went through it again. I have so much respect for what that took.

And there he was in December. Another boy, just as we’d hoped. Ready, I think, for this noisy family of ours. I look at him and think, what a good thing we decided to do.

Then there were four of us. I still smile when I say it. You and me and two little people we get to raise and watch grow.

Memory XIIBetween us

Interlude

A page of your own

I love the life we’ve made together. I’m cheering for the things you’re going after for yourself.

I hope you have the time and all the room you need to go after what matters to you.

12 / 13

Memory XIIIBetween us

A letter for you

I’d say yes again.

One photo. One yes. Look at us now. You and me and these two little people we get to love. My mom called it a proper circle. I’m so happy I said yes to you. I’d say it again in a heartbeat.

What happened will always be part of our story. It left a dent, and I’ll live with my part in it. I still feel it in the middle of an ordinary day, when a conversation we never quite finished comes back to me.

When you want company, I’ll run beside you. And if you look back and see me farther behind, that’s me in the car, with water packs and whatever else you need to keep going.

Be happy, stay happy, and live your life. Thank you for being together all these years. I’m so happy I get to share this life with you.

Happy anniversary.
